chunks: Sahl, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Fuzayl ibn Muyassar, who said:

We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man came and complained to him of a calamity that had befallen him. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Know that if you are patient, you will be rewarded; and if you are not patient, the decree of Allah which He has decreed upon you will still pass over you, and you will be excused (or burdened with sin depending on interpretation).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of being patient versus impatient during a calamity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the nuanced relationship between human agency and divine decree (*al-Qada*), distinguishing between the inevitability of the event and the moral weight of the response. He teaches that while the calamity itself is pre-ordained and thus inevitable, the choice to exercise *sabr* (patience) transforms the experience into a source of spiritual reward, whereas impatience leaves one accountable for their reaction. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *sabr* not merely as passive endurance, but as an active, volitional act of worship that aligns the believer with God's will.
